newsitem.title: USA: US spot natgas mostly higher on aftermarket demand.
newsitem.headline: US spot natgas mostly higher on aftermarket demand.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices wavered only slightly Monday as incremental demand pumped up prices in the Gulf but spring-like midwestern temperatures put some downward pressure on those prices, industry sources said.
Louisiana Gulf prices at the Henry Hub were talked an average of two cents higher at $2.20-2.24 per mmBtu despite the downward trend in futures.
At 1331 EDT, NYMEX's June Henry Hub gas futures were 5.2 cents lower at $2.215 per mmBtu.
Most other physical deals on the Gulf pipes were reported done around $2.20.

In the Northeast, New York city-gate prices gained two to three cents to the mid-to-high $2.40s as cooler weather headed toward the area. Warmer weather is forecast for Thursday, but a return of below-normal temperatures is expected this weekend, Weather Services Corp said.
Appalachian prices were up a similar amount to the mid-$2.30s to low-$2.40s on Columbia and CNG.
In the Midcontinent, where temperatures are hovering near to slightly below normal, prices eased by one to two cents to the high-$1.90s to about $2.
Chicago city-gate values were talked in the low-$2.30s, while Detroit city-gate gas sold in the mid-to-high $2.30s.

In west Texas, Permian prices gained two cents to about $1.93-1.96, while prices at the southern California border rose six cents to about $2.10. Most deals at Waha were reported done at $2.03 and $2.04.
Temperatures in the Southwest are expected to remain warmer-than-normal through this week, which will likely attract more buyers to the market to meet air conditioning demand.
